Title: Contact Recycling :: Box2D
Description:
Contact recycling is a technique I developed for Box2D and Box3D. Contact recycling can drastically improve rigid body simulation performance, making the process of computing contact points almost free. Further, recycling can significantly improve stability.
Contact recycling combines ideas from other techniques. I had not seen this specific technique used in other physics engines as of March 2026 when I added it to Box2D in this pull request. There are similar solutions to the same problem but they have some fundamental differences.

Title: Who is vfmaddrnd231pd??
Description:
vfmaddrnd231pd is a unique instruction from the FMA instruction set. Most instructions in that set have mnemonics like vfmadd231pd, but here rnd means something very specific. The Intel Software Development Manual documents it as:

VFMADDRND231PD – Fused Multiply-Add of Packed Double-Precision Floating-Point Values with rounding control
[…] The immediate byte defines several bit fields that control rounding, DAZ, FTZ, and exception suppression (See Table 5-3).

Title: Living in the Weimar era of Ruby
Description: Much has been said about the DHH keynote that he gave at RailsWorld. To me, it was the voice of a person in an existential crisis, but also a very jaded one. “Look how I don’t care anymore, and you should not care either” is not a great message when you are the headline speaker at the conference - let’s call it CareConf - that you have, yourself, lobbied for. The message from the supreme leader was clear: we vibe-rewrote HEY in a more performant way, it worked great, we neither need nor care about Rails anymore. I honestly believe that, instead of amassing even more applause via vitriolic truth-bombing, he could have just left the toy he no longer loves - including its community - in peace. But here is the thing: the rich and famous losing interest in the good stuff does not oblige the rest of us to. If anything, it frees up the room.
